record.what_it_does: Flexible, data-driven CRM for records, lists, workflows and relationship intelligence.
record.auth_notes: Attio recommends OAuth 2.0 (authorization code) for apps that serve multiple workspaces. User-level tokens require PKCE, which is optional for workspace-level tokens, and a workspace admin approves the app's scopes on install. For a single workspace, an API key (access token) can be generated on the app's developer settings page. Tokens are sent as Bearer in the Authorization header. HTTP Basic is also accepted, with the token as username and a blank password, though Bearer is recommended. The api_key and bearer_token entries describe the same static workspace token.
record.access_notes: The pricing page lists "API and webhooks" on every plan, including Free ($0, up to 3 users). Every plan also includes the Attio MCP server. SQL query access via the API or MCP is Ultra-only. A developer can create a workspace API key or an OAuth app without approval. An unpublished app can be installed in up to 25 workspaces, and private invite links show an "unreviewed" warning. Wider distribution means publishing to the App Store, and "Publishing requires a review from the Attio team, which can take up to 1 week."
record.api_breadth_notes: The REST API covers objects, attributes, records, lists, entries, notes, tasks, comments/threads, meetings, workspace members, webhooks and SCIM. llms.txt lists roughly 150 endpoint pages, or about 160 including SCIM. An OpenAPI spec is published.
record.mcp_notes: https://mcp.attio.com/mcp is hosted by Attio and uses OAuth login, with no API keys needed. It is included on every plan. The query-particle-sql tool is plan-gated (Ultra).
record.blocker_notes: API keys and OAuth apps are self-serve on the Free plan, so building and testing can start now. A multi-tenant OAuth app serving many users' workspaces goes past the 25-workspace limit for unpublished apps. That requires publishing to the Attio App Store, which involves an Attio team review (up to 1 week) and listing requirements.
